speaker: A. W. Tozer
title: Defenseless before the Lord
text: First of all he should put away all defense and make no attempt to excuse himself either in his own eyes or before the Lord. Whoever defends himself will have himself for his defense, and he will have no other; but let him come defenseless before the Lord and he will have for his defender no less than God Himself.
modern_interpretation: In a world that often demands we present a perfect front, this wisdom encourages radical vulnerability. It suggests that if you constantly try to defend your ego, justify your actions, or make excuses, you limit yourself to your own finite capabilities and flawed perspective. Instead, by dropping your guard, acknowledging your imperfections, and surrendering your need for self-preservation, you open yourself up to a powerful, divine support that far exceeds anything you could conjure on your own.
summary: Cease all self-defense and excuses, for relying on your own justification leaves you alone. Instead, come vulnerably before the Divine, and God Himself will become your ultimate defender.
actionable_advice: Practice radical honesty: for the next 24 hours, consciously observe and resist the urge to explain away your mistakes or justify your opinions, choosing instead to simply acknowledge them without defense.
embedding_ready_text: A. W. Tozer's 'Defenseless before the Lord' (Pursuit of God, Chapter 2) teaches that true strength comes from shedding our defenses and excuses. The original text states: 'First of all he should put away all defense and make no attempt to excuse himself either in his own eyes or before the Lord. Whoever defends himself will have himself for his defense, and he will have no other; but let him come defenseless before the Lord and he will have for his defender no less than God Himself.' This wisdom addresses emotional states like pride, shame, and fear of judgment, and common problems such as inability to admit fault or spiritual stagnation. It encourages profound vulnerability and surrender to a higher power, rather than relying solely on our limited ego-driven self-justifications. By letting go of the need to always be right or to protect our image, we open ourselves to divine grace and powerful support. This transformative guidance emphasizes humility, trust, and courage in acknowledging imperfection, leading to deeper spiritual connection and mental well-being.
